records.deidentified_narrative: at the listed date and time police responded to the report taken location for an accident major. upon arrival i made contact with u1d, who had relocated u1 to the nearby 7-eleven. u1d provided me with the following statement: u1 traveling eastbound on the [roadway] in the far left (#1) lane with the intent of turn left (northbound) [roadway]. u1d had a red signal light. u1d braked, but due to rainy weather conditions and wet roadways, u1 hydroplaned through the intersection. the front end of u1 struck the signal light pole on the northeast corner of the intersection. u1d denied that u1 hit ped. u1d did not complain of pain or injury. i made contact with ped, who provided me with the following statement: ped was standing on the sidewalk on the northeast corner of the intersection. u1 drove through the intersection and the front end of u1 struck both ped and the light pole. ped complained of left leg pain. ped was assessed by ems on scene, but not transported to a medical facility. w1 made contact with me and provided me with the following statement: w1 observed u1 hydroplane through the intersection while u1 was [roadway]. w1 observed the front end of u1 collide with ped and the light pole on the northeast corner of the intersection while ped was standing on the sidewalk. i observed a large dent on the metal signal light pole, but noted that the signal lights were still operable. info notified public works of the damage (reference # [phone]). u1's front bumper was on the ground next to the light pole. u1 had front end damage and the airbags were deployed. ofc n. swain #492 completed tsr [identifier] (mission towing) for u1 to be towed to growdon. the damage i observed was consistent with u1d/ped/w1's statements. u1d provided me with his identifying information and driver's license number. u1d told me that u1d did not have his driver's license with him. upon running u1d's information, i found that u1d had drivers license restriction b - licensed operator in front seat (lofs) 21 and older, however u1d had told me that u1d was the sole occupant of u1 at the time crash. ofc n. swain #492 issued u1d citation no. [identifier]. i also found that u1d had an active arrest warrant (reference sapd22246573). ofc b. christensen #1346 completed sapd form 12-dar for u1d/ped and provided each party with a [case id] and the other's information. i contacted sgt d. rodriguez #3003 (npb) and det a. stautzenberger #2506 (tid) for notification of this incident. bwc/coban available.

records.deidentified_narrative: unit #2 was a passenger car which had been traveling westbound on sh-256. however, unit #2 was currently disabled from a previous deer crash and was resting in the [roadway] with its hazard lights flashing. there was currently no lighting at the location of the crash. unit #1 was also traveling westbound on sh-256. the unit #1 driver noticed the flashing hazard lights of unit #2 up ahead of him, but he did not realize, at first, that it was a disabled stationary vehicle in the middle of the roadway. once he did realize this, the driver of unit #1 hit his brakes and swerved hard to the right in attempt to avoid collision. one of the female passengers from unit #2, now a pedestrian, was already out of the vehicle and trying to get the attention of the unit #1 driver to slow down. when she feared he was not going to stop, she called for the female driver and the front seat male passenger of unit #2 to hurriedly get out of the vehicle and head for the barrow ditch on the north side of sh-256. the unit #2 driver and passenger immediately did so, but this move proved fatal as the left side of unit #1 made parallel contact with the right side of unit #2. the male passenger in the front seat was partially ejected in the collision as he tried to exit at the moment unit #1 was making contact with unit #2. as a result, this male passenger sustained critical injuries. the female driver, now a pedestrian, was struck as she tried to run for the barrow ditch in front of units #2 and #1. she was later pronounced dead at the scene by the justice of the peace. after grazing the side of unit #2, unit #1 went deep into the northside barrow ditch where it received undercarriage damage and continued for a short distance before coming back up onto sh-256. unaware he had just struck a person, the driver of unit #1 continued westbound as he tried calling 911 near the scene. his call was not successful, so he continued traveling until he came to a gas station in memphis, tx which was about four miles west of the crash scene. here, the unit #1 driver made another 911 call, this time successful, and notified the local sheriff's department he had just been involved in a crash and where he was at. the unit #1 driver was uninjured. even though he should have stopped at the scene to see if any individuals had been hurt, further investigation revealed that the unit #1 driver never intended to flee the scene. after the collision, unit #2 appeared to remain close to its original position before the crash, upright and facing [roadway] of sh-256. unit #2 was towed from the scene while unit #1 was drivable. unit #2 sustained minor right-side distributed parallel damage from the impact while unit #1 received front left and undercarriage damage.

records.deidentified_narrative: unit 3 was stowed away inside the top open portion of unit 1 (top of tractor cab air dam). when unit 1 stopped at a red light unit 3 attempted to climb down from unit 1 and flee. the signal light turned green and unit 1 & 2 drove forward. unit 3 was caught between the cab and back tandem wheels (right side) and run over. unit 3 was pronounced deceased on scene at 2111 hours by horne#3402 (medic 18). medical examiner ryan #120 (me# 22-3122) responded to the scene to take custody of unit 3. tid detective davis #2406 and sgt westmoreland #3016 responded to the scene. csi stoever #2066 responded to the scene. **this report was supplemented on [date] by det. p. davis #2406 to add the toxicology results for unit 3. tx dot personnel incorrectly added that urine was drawn from unit 3 when it was actually blood that was drawn. unit 3's blood was positive for carbon monoxide (<10% cohb). the presence of carbon monoxide was consistent with unit 3 being a stowaway in the wind dam on top of unit 1.**

records.deidentified_narrative: on [date], around 2118 hours, princeton police officers were dispatched to [roadway]/[roadway] for a welfare check. while enroute to the area dispatch advised a female pedestrian was believed to be struck by a vehicle. upon arrival, officer observed approximately 15 vehicles in both lanes of travel. officer approached the scene. officer observed a female pedestrian located in the #2 [roadway] with several bystanders and a female conducting cpr on a female pedestrian. officers conducted cpr on the female pedestrian until ems arrived on scene. officers interviewed witnesses and the driver of unit 1. witnesses stated a partially clothed female pedestrian was walking in [roadway]. a witness stated her and her husband were driving east in the [roadway]. they observed the female walking in the [roadway]. female and her husband stated they made a u turn and traveled in #1 [roadway]. the couple put their hazards on to check on the female. at that time unit 2 was traveling in #2 lane and the female pedestrian walked into #2 lane causing unit 1 to collide with the female pedestrian. upon interviewing the driver of unit 1, he stated he was traveling in #2 lane and observed the vehicle make a u turn and turn its hazards on. he observed the vehicle with its hazards on complete the u turn and he decelerated. he then accelerated to continue to travel past the vehicle. as he was passing the vehicle the female pedestrian walked into #2 lane in front of his vehicle and he struck the pedestrian with the center and right front portion of the vehicle. unit 1 driver pulled over on to the shoulder and called 911, he advised 911 dispatch of the incident. witnesses on scene confirmed female pedestrian entered the roadway in front of unit 1. the female was transported to medical city of mckinney by ems. the vehicle was towed by 1st choice towing. officer later spoke to staff at medical city of mckinney and advised of fatal injuries.
